summary.text: Acknowledgements for the Spanish edition, explaining that the document draws on a technical consultation on sexual and reproductive health and HPV vaccination programmes held in Montreux, Switzerland, on 14–16 March 2006, and listing the participating experts and WHO departments.

sections.extract: Este documento se basa en los resultados de las deliberaciones de una reunión consultiva técnica titulada “Programas de salud sexual y reproductiva y de vacunación contra el VPH”, que tuvo lugar del 14 al 16 de marzo de 2006 en Montreux, Suiza. sections.title: Page 6

summary.text: Introduces the guidance, in Spanish, explaining that it comes from a UNFPA–WHO consultation and is meant to inform those working in sexual and reproductive health, immunization, adolescent health and cancer control about HPV vaccine introduction. It describes the burden of cervical cancer and notes that wide screening coverage has greatly reduced deaths in high-income countries.

sections.extract: Este documento de orientación se basa en los resultados de las deliberaciones de una reunión consultiva técnica titulada “Programas de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva y de Vacunación contra el VPH”, organizada conjuntamente por el UNFPA y la OMS, que tuvo lugar en marzo de 2006 en Montreux, Suiza. summary.text: Describes, in Spanish, the two prophylactic HPV vaccines, which trials showed to be highly effective in women aged 16–24 not previously exposed to the virus, and notes that HPV types 16 and 18 cause 70% of cervical cancers. It reports the licensing status of Gardasil and the expected approval of Cervarix in 2006.

summary.text: Notes, in Spanish, that follow-up of phase III trial participants continues to answer open questions relevant to vaccination programmes, such as duration of protection, and includes a figure on HPV types in women with cancer by region.

sections.title: Page 10

summary.text: Explains, in Spanish, that HPV vaccines are expected to be licensed first for girls and women aged 9–26, with stronger immune responses in younger girls. It notes that effects in women over 25 or already infected with types 16 or 18 still need study and that cost-effectiveness for these groups is unknown.

sections.extract: Según las indicaciones disponibles en la actualidad, la comercialización de las vacunas contra el VPH se autorizará inicialmente para su administración a niñas y mujeres de 9 a 26 años de edad. sections.title: Page 11

summary.text: Links HPV vaccination, in Spanish, to WHO's 2004 Global Reproductive Health Strategy and its core aspects of sexual and reproductive health. It notes that, unlike vaccines such as rubella or tetanus, HPV vaccines will draw immunization programmes into sensitive issues of adolescent sexuality.

summary.text: Summarizes, in Spanish, the UNICEF–WHO Global Immunization Vision and Strategy, which aims by 2015 for immunization to be a high priority and equitably available to all ages. It notes that efforts to prevent and control cervical cancer have so far been limited.

sections.extract: Visión y Estrategia Mundial de Inmunización del UNICEF y la OMS La 58ª Asamblea Mundial de la Salud aprobó la Visión y Estrategia Mundial de Inmuni- zación, preparada por el UNICEF y la OMS. sections.title: Page 14

summary.text: Argues, in Spanish, that experience introducing HPV vaccines could serve as a model for a future HIV vaccine and is relevant to the HIV community. It discusses the unique opportunity and high cost of HPV vaccines, warning that private-sector introduction could favour better-off groups and high- and middle-income countries.

sections.extract: La experiencia que se adquirirá con la introducción de las vacunas contra el VPH podría servir de modelo para la eventual vacuna contra el virus de inmunodeﬁ ciencia humana (VIH); además, la prevención y el tratamiento del cáncer cervicouterino en las mujeres inmunodeﬁ cientes también resultarán de interés para la comunidad dedicada al VIH. De ese modo, se atenderán las recomendaciones del Llamamiento de Nueva York

sections.title: Page 15

summary.text: Warns, in Spanish, that uneven introduction could widen health inequities, calling for strong public–private partnerships. It discusses how vaccination strategy must reflect each country's circumstances and the possible delays between licensing, affordable pricing and adequate supply in developing countries.

En todos los contextos será necesario crear fuertes alianzas entre los sectores público y privado para evitarlo. summary.text: Discusses, in Spanish, the challenges of designing balanced advocacy, information and communication on HPV vaccination for varied audiences. It lists key facts to convey, such as that most HPV infections cause no symptoms and can be passed on unknowingly.

sections.extract: La preparación de programas de sensibilización, información y comunicación sobre la vacunación contra el VPH, dirigidos a interesados directos y públicos muy distintos, comprende problemáticas y oportunidades especíﬁ cas. sections.title: Page 17

summary.text: Continues the key messages, in Spanish, noting that the vaccines are highly effective in unexposed women aged 16–26 and expected to prevent up to 70% of cervical cancers, best given before first sexual contact. It stresses that national data on cervical cancer burden, HPV types and age at first sex should guide policy.

sections.extract: • Las vacunas proﬁ lácticas contra el VPH son sumamente eﬁ caces en las mujeres de 16 a 26 años que nunca han estado expuestas a ese virus y se espera que prevengan hasta un 70% de cánceres cervicouterinos en las mujeres vacunadas. • Probablemente, el efecto máximo de las vacunas contra el VPH se obtendrá administrándolas antes de la primera relación sexual. • Ambas vacunas contra el VPH también pueden proteger

sections.title: Page 18

summary.text: Sets out, in Spanish, the elements of a communication strategy on cervical cancer control and HPV vaccines aimed at decision makers, health professionals, women and communities, timed to national decisions. It lists what information to give target groups, such as indications, safety and side-effects.

sections.extract: • Una estrategia de comunicación sobre el control del cáncer cervical en general, y las vacunas contra el VPH en particular, que debería estar dirigida a los interesados directos y los responsables de la adopción de decisiones clave, así como a los profesionales de la salud, las mujeres y la comunidad. summary.text: Continues the communication guidance, in Spanish, stressing that vaccination does not imply stigma or that a girl is sexually active and setting out what is still unknown, such as use in women with HIV or pregnant women. It suggests linking messages to existing adolescent programmes such as school-based sexual health, nutrition, tobacco and HIV prevention education.

sections.title: Page 20

summary.text: Discusses, in Spanish, reaching target groups, with a likely licensed age range of 9–26 divided into a priority group of girls aged 9–13 and a catch-up group. It weighs delivery through schools, health services and community programmes, including challenges in extending the cold chain to adolescent programmes.

sections.extract: Llegar a los grupos diana Probablemente, la edad de administración de las vacunas a los grupos diana que se establecerá en la autorización de comercialización estará comprendida entre los 9 y los 26 años. Ese grupo de edad deberá subdividirse en dos categorías: una prioritaria y otra “de repesca”. summary.text: Continues the discussion of service delivery, in Spanish, noting that staff of youth programmes may lack vaccination skills but that programmes for out-of-school youth can raise awareness and refer young people to vaccination services. It suggests using contacts such as prevention of mother-to-child HIV transmission services to inform women about cervical cancer, HPV vaccines and screening.

sections.extract: Además, el personal de esos programas puede carecer de las competencias necesarias para prestar servicios de vacunación. summary.text: Stresses, in Spanish, that older women outside the vaccine's age limits still need comprehensive cervical cancer screening, diagnosis and treatment, and that vaccinated girls must also be screened later. It begins discussing the need to plan monitoring and evaluation from the preparatory stage.

sections.extract: En las autorizaciones de comercialización de las vacunas contra el VPH se establecerán los límites de edad máximo y mínimo de administración a la población diana. summary.text: Continues the list of actions, in Spanish, such as extending immunization services to older age groups, aligning messages with cervical cancer, adolescent health and HIV programmes, monitoring vaccine effectiveness, training health workers and defining process and outcome indicators.

sections.title: Page 25

summary.text: Discusses, in Spanish, stewardship and financing, giving high priority to mobilizing international and national resources to strengthen health systems and buy HPV vaccines as part of a comprehensive multi-partner strategy. It notes that national decisions should consider benefits not captured in health and cost analyses.

sections.extract: La movilización de recursos para reforzar el sistema de atención de la salud y adquirir vacunas contra el VPH, tanto en el plano internacional, como en los presupuestos de salud de los países, deberá tener una alta prioridad. sections.title: Page 26

summary.text: Stresses, in Spanish, the importance of international funding commitments for HPV vaccines through GAVI, UNICEF and the PAHO Revolving Fund, to encourage manufacturers to expand production capacity and to lower prices. It also covers regulatory tasks after licensing, such as adverse event reporting by the private sector and pharmacovigilance.

summary.text: Lists, in Spanish, actions on stewardship and financing, such as forming a national working group with broad stakeholder participation to prepare an HPV vaccine introduction strategy and planning for financial sustainability. Countries not eligible for GAVI funding are advised to seek WHO and UNFPA technical help.

sections.title: Page 28

summary.text: Concludes, in Spanish, that the decision on whether and when to introduce HPV vaccination rests with national policies and that effective alliances are needed because the vaccines span several programmes. It ends with a note on the conditions for which the quadrivalent vaccine was licensed by the US FDA.

sections.extract: En última instancia, la decisión relativa a la introducción de la vacunación contra el VPH, así como a la fecha en que se hará, dependerán de las políticas nacionales de cada país. La importancia que se concederá a la vacuna contra el VPH dentro de una estructura global e integrada de vacunación constituye una consideración general.
